newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom set to build huge Jakarta tower.
newsitem.headline: Telkom set to build huge Jakarta tower.

text.p: Indonesian telecommunication companies PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) and PT Indonesia Satellite Corp (Indosat) said on Monday that they had set up a joint venture company to build a 558 metre-high telecommunications tower in Jakarta.

"Telkom together with PT Indosat Mega Media (a subsidiary of Indosat), a unit of state broadcaster TVRI and PT Indocitra Grahabawana have signed agreements to set up a joint venture company PT Menara Jakarta," Telkom said in a statement.
Menara Jakarta will build the tower, which will be among the tallest of its kind in the world.
Telkom and Indosat have a 20 percent stake each in the company, TVRI nine percent and Indocitra a 51 percent stake.

The Jakarta tower is expected to cost about $560 million to build and would still need foreign investors, the statement said. "In the near future there will be a new joint venture company involving foreign partners," the statement said. It did not elaborate.
A source at Indocitra said the tower would be mainly for telecommunications but would also include retail and tourism services.
The source, who asked not to be named, said it was too early to give a time-frame for the construction as the joint-venture company had just been set up.
